Malaysia will continue to work constructively with other member states through the intergovernmental negotiations on the Security Council reform towards improving the United Nations to make it more efficient, open, transparent and inclusive. Thank you, President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Malaysia. And now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Norway.

President, last Thursday, this Assembly overwhelmingly adopted a resolution calling for a ceasefire and humanitarian access to Gaza. Fourteen members of the Security Council agree with the General Assembly. Norway therefore strongly regrets that the Security Council, again, failed to pronounce itself on this issue. With the latest regional escalation, we call for restraint by the parties involved and for respect for international law. Now, more than ever, we need to keep focused on the civilians in Gaza and the West Bank. They must not be forgotten. Israel has for more than three months severely restricted access for humanitarian aid, including food, medicine, and fuel to Gaza. The inhumane conditions imposed on the civilians in Gaza are unacceptable. OCHA warns us that the Gaza Strip can enter full-fledged famine by September. This must end now. Women in Gaza are disproportionately impacted. Women, peace and security commitments must also be upheld. President, using starvation as a method of warfare and killing civilians seeking aid is a violation of international law and Norway strongly opposes it. As an occupying power, Israel is obliged to ensure that humanitarian aid reaches all the population in need. Norway demands the immediate and permanent facilitation of full, rapid, safe, and unhindered entry and movement of humanitarian assistance throughout Gaza. The UN and humanitarian organizations operating in accordance with humanitarian principles must be allowed to do their job. Norway continues to call on both parties to agree to an immediate ceasefire. The only way to stop the suffering of civilians in Gaza and secure the release of all the hostages remaining is to stop the war. as a two-state solution is the only way to end the conflict and secure long-lasting peace and security for Palestinians and Israelis alike. Norway firmly opposes any measures that jeopardize the establishment of an independent Palestinian state and the viability of a two-state solution. Presently, more than 80% of Gaza is under Israeli military control or subject to evacuation orders. Increased settlement activities in the West Bank aim to consolidate Israeli control over Palestinian territory. These actions are in clear violation of international law. Norway welcomes the leadership of France and Saudi Arabia in chairing the high-level international UN conference on the peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution. President, I would like to end by thanking the presidency for the special report submitted pursuant to resolution 76262. Further to this, We encourage the President of the Assembly to send a summary from this debate back to the Security Council. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Norway. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Indonesia.

Mr. President, less than 24 hours after the adoption of resolution ES10/27, we witness yet again another violation of international law through Israel's unilateral attack against Iran. Indonesia strongly condemns such attack, which exacerbates an already fragile regional security situation. We urge all parties to exercise restraint. de-escalate tensions and return to the path of diplomacy. At the same time, we must continue to address the root cause of instability in the region, the occupation of the Palestinian people. It further underscores that military actions, whether against the people of Gaza, Syria, Lebanon, Yemen, or Iran, will never deliver the sense of security for all parties. Mr. President, we should not have needed to meet today, if the Security Council's decision-making reflects global conscience. We should not have needed to meet today if our multilateral system is truly based on humanity, justice, and international law. Yet once again, for the seventh time in 21 months, we have to reconvene the emergency session for the rest of the world to say, "Enough is enough." The fact that, on average, We have to meet once in every three months. reflect the continuing and systematic denial of the fundamental rights of the Palestinian people. A systematic denial often represented by a single raise of hand in the council chamber, leading to hundreds of additional deaths every day after. A systematic denial of an ongoing genocide, despite the fact that by now, more than one in every 40 Palestinians in Gaza have perished. We shall not be silenced. And Indonesia calls for all nations to join us in the following four actions. First, to ensure effective and full implementation of the resolution we adopted last week. The humanitarian situation in Gaza has reached a breaking point. This resolution and our support are a message of resolve of the world's conscience united against despicable atrocities. Second, to insist on a permanent ceasefire in Gaza. Every delay of the ceasefire will be measured in children lost, hospitals destroyed, cycles of violence perpetuated. We must all be loud and clear to demand a ceasefire along with full, safe, unhindered humanitarian access and distribution. Third, to reaffirm the primacy of international law. We must all be alarmed by the continued blatant defiance of international law, UN resolutions, the binding orders of the ICJ, and its advisory opinions. Humanitarian workers targeted, aid continuously blocked, UNRWA dismantled, starvation used as a method of warfare. These are all systematic, deliberate, grave breaches of Geneva Conventions. And this set a dangerous precedent to the current world order, an attempt to establish a global order based on the might is right. We must all be firm. Accountability is not optional and impunity is not an option. And finally, we must revive and sustain the path to peace. Indonesia reaffirms our unwavering commitment to the two-state solution, in accordance with international agreed parameters and relevant UN resolutions. The failure of the Security Council has brought us here, but this General Assembly must now become a catalyst for progress, a beacon of hope. While Indonesia regrets the postponement of the high-level conference on the two-state solution, we remain committed to its convening, and we are honored to serve as co-chair of the roundtable on security alongside Italy. It is vital that we maintain the momentum to implement the two-state solution as the only viable path to peace. Expectations are high that the conference will become a watershed moment, preserve the political horizon, and anchor a future of peace and stability in the region. Mr. President, our meeting is a testament that in the darkest of times, the vast majority of nations stand firm for justice, peace, and the rule of law. We must continue our steps towards ending the occupation and restoring the rights and dignity of the Palestinian people. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Indonesia, and now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Pakistan.

Mr. President, we thank you for continuing the debate in this resumed session of the 10th Emergency Special Session. pursuant to the joint request of the Arab Group and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. We meet amid profound anguish and disappointment and mounting human despair. Despite broad support for a principled, balanced, and humanitarian draft resolution on Gaza, that was advanced by the 10 elected members of the Security Council, including Pakistan, it was vetoed. Once again, a vital opportunity to uphold the UN Charter and our collective responsibility was lost. In such moments, the responsibility of this General Assembly, the most representative and democratic organ of the United Nations, is magnified. It must speak where the Council has been prevented from acting. The resolution adopted by this Assembly last week entitled Protection of Civilians and Upholding Legal and Humanitarian Obligations was a necessary assertion of international will. Pakistan is proud to have supported and co-sponsored this initiative. The resolution calls for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, release of hostages, condemns the weaponization of starvation, demands unimpeded humanitarian access, and insists on accountability and compliance with international law. Moreover, the resolution recalls that this is a situation of illegal occupation. and reiterates the obligations of Israel, the occupying power, under international law. These are not mere aspirations. They are, in fact, obligations. The international community must act with urgency to ensure their implementation. President, the situation in Gaza is a stain on our collective conscience. Over 55,000 lives have been lost. including 18,000 children and 28,000 women. Infrastructure has been razed. Homes, hospitals, schools, cultural heritage, places of worship, nothing has been spared. Famine looms. Humanitarian workers and UN personnel are being attacked with impunity. This is not just a humanitarian catastrophe. It is a collapse of humanity. Against this backdrop, Pakistan reiterates the immediate steps necessary not only to stem this horror, but to lay the foundations for a just and lasting peace. First, an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire. Resolution 2735 of the Security Council must be implemented in full. The killing must stop now. Second, the full and unconditional lifting of the Gaza blockade. Humanitarian aid must flow freely and safely. International agencies must be empowered, not hindered. Third, the full restoration of UNRWA's mandate, access, and funding. It is indispensable to the survival and dignity of the Palestinian people. Attempts to politicize or undermine and delegitimize under war are deeply counterproductive and must end. Fourth, and most critically, we must confront the root cause, the prolonged illegal Israeli occupation of Palestinian lands. There will be no durable peace without justice, and no justice without the realization of the two-state solution. based on pre-1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as the capital of a sovereign, independent, and contiguous state of Palestine. In this regard, Pakistan looks forward to the reconvening of the high-level conference on Palestine and the two-state solution in coming weeks to be chaired by France and Saudi Arabia. We must work together to ensure its tangible outcomes in advancing a credible path towards peace, Palestinian statehood, and Palestine's full membership of the United Nations. It will be yet another clear demonstration of where the international community stands on this issue. President, the stakes could not be higher. The international community must not look away. The credibility of the international system, in fact, of multilateralism itself, is on trial. It is indeed ludicrous that the occupying power, the worst violator of international law, and those who protect and shield it can stand in this august assembly criticizing and blaming the rest of the international community for being on the right side of history. Moral bankruptcy must have no space in this house. We must rise above politics and pressure and act with moral clarity, legal integrity, and political will. We must condemn aggression. Pakistan's commitment to the Palestinian people is unwavering. We stand with them in their rightful struggle for dignity, self-determination, and peace. We will continue to raise our voice in solidarity and in hope until justice is done, until the occupation is ended, and their inalienable rights are realized. That is in line with the permanent responsibility of the United Nations with regard to the question of Palestine until it is resolved in all its aspects in accordance with international law and the relevant UN resolutions. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Pakistan and now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Cuba.

Thank you, President. President, once again, We see double standards that appear to be unlimited, as the Government of the United States is on the wrong side of history. With its recent vote, quite alone, that country doesn't just prevent the Security Council from acting, it also hinders the steps that could be taken to achieve peace and to protect civilians in Palestine. If the US is really interested in contributing to mediation efforts to reach a permanent and lasting ceasefire, it would immediately stop its political, military, logistical and financial support to Israel. And it would not allow it to continue its plans to exterminate the Palestinian civilian population. With its anti democratic veto power, far from upholding international peace and security, it once again provides protection and impunity to Israel, the occupying power. Its complicity with genocide against the Palestinian people marks one of the saddest and most shameful chapters in the history of humanity. President, how many more innocent lives of civilians, including women and children, have to happen? and this includes in the context of the apartheid and crimes against humanity against the Palestinians how many more of these things have to happen for the international community to act. We cannot turn a blind eye to the massacre that Israel is continuing against the Palestinians as well as the systematic bombing and destruction of civilian infrastructure. We denounce the continued occupation of Palestinian land and expulsion of Palestinians from their land. The Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territories including East Jerusalem have no legal basis whatsoever and they are a violation of international law. We can't achieve peace in the Middle East without a broad lasting and just settlement to the Palestinian question. We need to have an immediate permanent ceasefire in Gaza. We need to have a two-state solution that allows the people of Palestine to have an independent and sovereign state within the pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital. And refugees need to have the right to return to their land. In addition to this, Palestine must be admitted as a fully fledged member of the United Nations without further delay. The occupying power needs urgently to allow the provision of sufficient humanitarian aid to the Palestinians and the vital work of UNRWA needs to be authorised. We hope that the high level conference and the implementation of a two state solution will be held as soon as possible. We regret the fact that this has been postponed as a result of Israel's attacks on Iran, clearly violating the UN Charter and international law and the principles of sovereignty and the threat or use of force against any other state. Israel's aggressive policy and its irresponsible actions are only possible thanks to the support given to it by the Government of the United States. This jeopardizes regional and international security and stability with unpredictable consequences for all of humanity. We stand in solidarity with the people and government of the Islamic Republic of Iran. We are concerned about the danger of a further escalation in the region and we call on the international community, particularly the General Assembly and the Security Council, to uphold their responsibility to uphold international peace and security and immediately to put an end to this aggression and impunity that Israel enjoys. The Palestinian cause will always have the unwavering solidarity of the Cuban people. Palestinians deserve to live in peace. Let us act now to change the course of history and to put an end once and for all to this genocide. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Cuba and now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Colombia.

Thank you, President. We'd like to thank the League of Arab States and the OIC for convening this meeting, which is really urgent. My delegation aligns itself with the statement delivered by Uganda on behalf of the NAM. Over the last 614 days in the Gaza Strip, more than 54,000 people have been killed, most of them women, children, and older persons. More than 14,000 people have disappeared or are assumed to be dead, and more than 125,000 have been injured. More than 210 journalists have been killed as they carried out their work. UN staff are constantly being targeted by the IDF, who have even opened fire on medical and humanitarian convoys. In the last three months, more than 640,000 people have been displaced on many occasions. 82% of the Gaza Strip is under militarized zones and under displacement orders. The internet in the Gaza Strip is totally cut off with negative consequences for all. In the midst of the largest starvation and extermination campaign in recent history, Israel has decided to block the entry of all humanitarian aid to Gaza. It's unacceptable that the UN, which was established precisely to protect future generations from the scourge of war, cannot find a consensus to act in these circumstances. And it's even more unacceptable that the Security Council, which has the primary responsibility to uphold international peace and security, is still silent in the face of a genocide taking place. The resolution put forward by the 10 elected members of the council on the 4th of June only sought to reiterate a call for a ceasefire, the immediate release of all hostages by Hamas and other groups, and for the entry of humanitarian assistance into Gaza. All of this is in line with the resolutions of the Council itself and international humanitarian law. But even though it was only a draft with only eight paragraphs, which just respected a minimum for all members, once again, the Council was blocked from acting as a result of a veto cast by a permanent member. It's really hard to understand what possible justification there can be to oppose a call for humanitarian assistance to get into Gaza when 2.1 million people are currently at risk of acute food insecurity, according to OCHA's statistics. In addition to intensifying suffering for millions of people, the lack of the Council action sends a worrying message in terms of giving the green lights to impunity and double standards, which erode the foundations of the multilateral system. Some members of this organization constantly are calling up, mentioning the fact that the usefulness of the UN has been called into question. What really jeopardizes our work is the incapacity of the UN to act and the veto cast to block the council from acting, which ignores international law, the purposes and principles of the charter, and goes against the most basic principles of humanity. President Petro has been crystal clear. Colombia will not be complicit in any genocide, any war crimes, or in supporting any apartheid regime in the 21st century. We are hopeful seeing that many countries are being clear that they endorse these, that they are acting in line with the same principles. We have to come up with a response to what is going on in Gaza. As signatories to the Charter, we have to do this and that is why we voted in favour of the resolution. It is a resolution that contains the most pressing measures to be taken to end the violence in Gaza and the occupied Palestinian territory. We hope that the high level conference will resume as soon as possible to implement the two state solution. The plight of millions of people in Palestine seems somewhat helpless, and the first step to end violence is to recognise that there will not be peace and security until the illegal occupation ceases. and that the starting point must be the implementation of a two-state solution with Israel and Palestine living side by side in internationally recognized borders pre-1967, with both peoples having the right to self-determination. We welcome the efforts undertaken by Egypt, Qatar and the United States to achieve a ceasefire, and we hope that they will soon lead to a positive outcome. We strongly condemn the use of hunger as a method of war. This is a war crime, and we call on the all parties, as the Security Council and the ICJ have done, to comply with international law. We stand in solidarity with the people of Palestine. There needs to be an immediate, permanent and unconditional ceasefire. All hostages need to be unconditionally immediately released and all human remains need to be returned. There needs to be an immediate unconditional delivery of humanitarian aid and the and all measures hindering UNRWA's work needs to be lifted. We will be judged on our position in these circumstances. In line with our historic position, we will continue to defend multilateralism and we will seek ways of having a fair solution to the question of Palestine, which will allow the peoples of Palestine and Israel to live side by side in peace and security. Together with South Africa, we convened a ministerial meeting on the 15th and 16th of July, which will be in Bogota. The aim will be to adopt diplomatic measures to respond to Israel's continued violations of international law, including the crime of genocide. We urge all states to join this effort and to adopt all measures that are necessary to stop this barbarism. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Colombia. And now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Malta.

We thank the chairs of the Arab Group and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation Group for requesting the resumption of the tenth emergency special session of the General Assembly, and we value the urgency with which this matter has been brought before us. We are meeting today because the Security Council could not agree on the resolution that would address the plight of the civilians in Gaza. We are meeting once more with the moral and political necessity of calling for an immediate ceasefire and watch on as a catastrophe continues to unfold before our eyes. We are meeting again faced with the collective responsibility of providing civilians with the humanitarian aid that they so desperately need, or taking a step back while the needs of Palestinians are weaponized and privatized. We are meeting again because, once more, we are stuck standing by idly while the world moves on, while the situation in Gaza continues to spiral towards an ever more dystopian reality. President, the vetoed resolution that brings us together today called for a concise set of deliverables. an immediate and permanent ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and unrestricted entry and access of humanitarian aid. These are aspirations that should not be controversial, and they are fully consistent with the position taken by Malta since the outbreak of hostilities, as well as the positions taken by the vast majority of Member States. We therefore reaffirm our call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire alongside so many others who have already spoken here today. Since 7 October 2023, Malta has consistently called for the unconditional release of all hostages captured by Hamas, expressing our sympathy for their families and loved ones. We have repeatedly condemned the horrific terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas, and we shall continue to condemn such behavior unequivocally. Nonetheless, we also condemn the weaponization, obstruction, and politicization of humanitarian aid. We condemn the collective punishment of civilians. This should not be a controversial point. We are deeply disappointed that even the bare minimum in terms of the observance of IHL has become too much to ask. In closing, the postponed high-level conference on the two-state solution takes on increased relevance in this context. Malta underscores its firm position that de-escalation and dialogue are fundamental elements to cultivate the necessary environment to relaunch negotiations for a just, comprehensive and peaceful resolution of this conflict based on the two-state solution along the pre-1967 borders. To this end, we reiterate the call for a ceasefire, the unconditional release of hostages, and the resumption of humanitarian aid to the population of Gaza in good faith as an essential step precisely towards the path of de-escalation, dialogue, and peace in the Middle East. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Malta and now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Turkey.

Mr. President, excellencies, distinguished delegates, Turkey welcomes convening of the 10th emergency special session of the General Assembly upon the request of the OIC and Arab groups. We gather once again in this hall under the shadow of a deepening crisis in Gaza, following the recent veto at the Security Council of a resolution that sought to address the unfolding catastrophic humanitarian situation. This also comes in parallel with Israel's attacks on Iran, an act that constitutes a flagrant violation of international law, especially UN Charter. We welcome adoption of the resolution entitled Protection of Civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations with 149 votes. This resolution is a reaffirmation of fundamental legal and moral principles and opportunity for the General Assembly to act where the Security Council has failed. Mr. President, humanitarian crisis in Gaza, Gaza Strip, has reached an unbearable magnitude. More than two million people are enduring unimaginable sufferings amid widespread destruction, starvation, and systematic denial of humanitarian assistance. Basic services have collapsed. Famine looms. Conditions of life are rapidly deteriorating, and international humanitarian law continues to be gravely violated. The crisis in Gaza has evolved beyond a mere humanitarian emergency. It constitutes a profound test of our collective humanity and moral obligation. There has been no safe and significant aid delivered in Gaza for more than three months now. The only way to do it is through the UN, including UNRWA. We categorically reject alternative models of aid delivery that compromise impartiality and dignity. The tragic loss of lives in the pursuit of aid tragically illustrates the human cost of misguided attempts. Humanitarian assistance is not a political concession. It is a legal and moral obligation. Aid must be delivered promptly, adequately, and without obstruction, through all available crossings and in accordance with the international humanitarian law and in coordination with the United Nations. The humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence must be respected. We call on the international community to move beyond statements of concern and take decisive, coordinated action. In this spirit, Turkey welcomes adoption of the draft resolution which we have co-sponsored. While the resolution could have reflected a more balanced perspective, particularly in operative paragraph two, where a reference to the immediate, dignified, and unconditional release of all Palestinian detainees held by Israel would have been appropriate, we nevertheless consider it an important and meaningful step forward. This resolution demands immediate, sustained, and unimpeded flow of humanitarian aid, including food, medical supplies, fuel, shelter, and access to clean water throughout Gaza, in coordination with the United Nations. It reaffirms support for UNRWA and underscores its indispensable role in alleviating sufferings on the ground. It also reiterates our collective commitment to a two-state solution and firmly rejects all attempts to alter the demographic or territorial status of the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem and Gaza. This point bears particular relevance. Turkey co-chairs a roundtable at the high-level international conference for the peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution, which will be held at the soonest possible convenience. We encourage all member states to seize the opportunity to invigorate efforts towards a just, comprehensive, and lasting peace. We commend the leadership of Saudi Arabia and France in steering this crucial process and call for meaningful steps to translate the two-state vision into reality. Mr. President, Turkey has long advocated for a reformed, democratic, representative, and effective Security Council. The recent veto of a similar resolution in the Security Council aimed at halting hostilities and facilitating humanitarian access is deeply regrettable. Use of veto in this context, in the face of such human suffering, stands in stark contrast to the will of the overwhelming majority of the member states and undermines credibility and effectiveness of the Council in fulfilling its responsibilities. It is precisely for moments like this that the General Assembly must act, guided by the moral weight of multilateral consensus and the urgency of human need. Adoption of this resolution is not merely a declaration of principle; it is a call to action. We send a united and resounding message, which means the international community will not tolerate impunity will not accept collective punishment, will not abandon the Palestinian civilian population, will not forget the atrocities and violations. We will not stand by as the international law is trampled and human suffering deepens. Turkey will continue to stand with the Palestinian people until a political solution based on the two-state vision and pre-1967 borders with East Jerusalem as the capital of an independent, sovereign, and geographically contiguous state of Palestine is achieved. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Turkey. And now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Brazil.

Mr. President, Brazil welcomed the adoption of the resolution Protection of Civilians and Upholding Legal and Humanitarian Obligations. It responds with moral clarity and legal grounding to the appalling humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip and in the occupied Palestinian territory. The resolution is a necessary step to protect the lives and dignity of civilians who continue to bear the brunt of Israel's repeated violations of international law. We gladly co-sponsored it. We must, however, express our deep frustration at the persistent failure of the Security Council in dealing with the conflict in Gaza. Despite the urgency of the current situation, meaningful action has been repeatedly obstructed. Once again, the General Assembly has had to act not by preference, but by necessity. The situation in the state of Palestine, particularly in Gaza, is of alarming gravity. The authorization mechanism imposed by Israel, which has been unequivocally rejected by humanitarian agencies, has dismantled humanitarian coordination and left over 2 million Palestinians without essential aid. Attacks on distribution sites have resulted in civilian deaths and further deepened the crisis. We therefore welcome the resolution's condemnation of the use of starvation as a method of warfare and its call for the immediate, safe, and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance in line with humanitarian principles and under the coordination of UN agencies. They have the required expertise to provide the much needed help in a dignified manner. Brazil also welcomes the resolution's reaffirmation of support for UNRWA. The agency's role remains irreplaceable. The deaths of over 300 staff since October 2023 are a tragic reminder of the risks faced by humanitarian personnel. As Vice Chair of UNRWA's Advisory Commission, soon to assume the chair, Brazil reaffirms its unwavering support for the agency and calls for strengthened international backing so it may continue fulfilling its mandate without interference. Mr. President, at some point in the near future, we'll reconvene to address the question of Palestine and the two-state solution. Brazil is honored to have co-chaired alongside Senegal Working Group Seven of the upcoming conference dedicated to promoting respect for international law. We hope the conference will mark a turning point, allowing us to look beyond the urgency and toward long-term recovery and reconstruction led by Palestinians themselves. By reaffirming its longstanding commitment to a two-state solution with an independent and viable state of Palestine living side by side with Israel in peace and security within the 1967 borders and with East Jerusalem as its capital, we reiterate our unwavering support for Palestine's quest for broader international recognition through legitimate diplomatic channels. there is no legal or political justification to continue denying the state of Palestine full membership in the United Nations. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Brazil. And now I give the floor to the distinguished representative of Jordan.

I thank you, Mr. President. First, My delegation would like to associate itself with the statement delivered by the Arab Group and the Non-Aligned Movement in New York. And allow me, Mr. President, to express our gratitude to you for responding to the request to resume the 10th emergency session -- emergency special session of the General Assembly. Jordan condemns the continued Israeli aggression on Gaza. and the humanitarian unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe it is causing for more than 2 million Palestinians who are besieged Jordan calls for an immediate and permanent ceasefire and the adequate and continued entry of humanitarian Aid to Gaza we confirm that the fact that Israel is halting the entry of humanitarian Aid is a grave violation of international humanitarian law Jordan calls for enabling United Nations agencies, especially UNRWA, to perform their duties with no obstacles. We confirm the need that these agencies must be able to provide basic services to more than five million refugees in its five areas of operation. Jordan renewed its support for the efforts exerted by the Egyptian Republic and Qatar and the United States to arrive at an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza. We also confirm our full support for convening the early recovery and reconstruction conference in Cairo as soon as a, an immediate ceasefire is reached and implementation of the resolutions of the emergency Arab summit. Mr. President, Jordan condemns the Israeli escalation and unilateral measures in the occupied West Bank, including the building of settlements, annexation of lands, and the continued and repeated incursions perpetrated by ministers in the Israeli government, as well as extremist settlers of the Al-Aqsa Mosque and Al-Haram Al-Qudsi, which are being conducted under the protection of the occupying forces. We stress that Israel has no sovereignty on East Jerusalem and its holy sites, and we warn of the gravity of these continued violations, we call upon the international community to shoulder its responsibilities and ensure their immediate halt. We also confirm that these Israeli violations of Islamic and Christian holy sites are considered a blatant violation of the historical and legal status quo of Jerusalem and is a violation of Israel's obligations as the occupying power. Moreover, the Al-Quds Awqaf Affairs, which is part of the Jordanian Islamic Holy Shrines Department, is the only department that is tasked with managing the holy Jerusalem campus, Al-Haram Al-Quds Al-Sharif, and arranging entry into it under the Hashemite guardianship of Islamic and Christian holy sites in the holy city. Mr. President, Jordan reaffirms its position supporting the rights of the Palestinian people that are inalienable, especially their established right in establishing an independent and sovereign state on the 4 June 1967 lines with East Jerusalem as their capital and based on the two-state solution and the Arab Peace Initiative. We stress that achieving peace and stability in the region cannot be achieved without putting an end to the occupation and without the embodiment of a Palestinian state, and we confirm that international recognition of the Palestinian state is not only a legal obligation but is a political and moral necessity as well. In closing, Jordan renews its support for the high-level international conference on the peaceful resolution of the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution. And we will contribute to its success and build upon its outcomes under the joint leadership of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the French Republic. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Jordan and now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Portugal.

Mr. President, despite the recent and very concerning escalation in the Middle East, we should also keep our focus on the grave humanitarian situation in Gaza. Portugal is deeply disappointed that the use of veto has injured the Security Council from speaking with one voice about the humanitarian situation in Gaza. While rooted in the UN Charter, the veto power carries a special responsibility. When used repeatedly to block Council action in the face of mass human suffering, it risks eroding the legitimacy of the Security Council and the trust that Member States and global citizens place in multilateral governance. The veto must not become a shield for inaction, particularly when the Council is called upon to address pressing humanitarian and security issues. Portugal reiterates its support for greater accountability in the use of the veto. including through the initiatives adopted by this Assembly, we call once again for wider adherence to the ACT Group's Code of Conduct and the Franco-Mexican Initiative, both of which aim to ensure that the veto is not exercised in situations involving atrocity crimes. As we mark the 80th anniversary of the United Nations, this is the time to renew our collective commitment to a Security Council that is more representative, transparent, and responsive to those it serves. Portugal supported and co-sponsored the resolution adopted last week. The General Assembly took a clear stance in demanding full respect for international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians, the immediate unconditional release of hostages, and the unimpeded humanitarian aid to Gaza. We support the calls made by the Secretary-General of the United Nations and other representatives of the UN system on the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip and in the West Bank. Now, our most pressing priority is to save lives and to show our compassion for the civilian bearing the brunt of this protracted conflict. it is imperative to protect Palestinian civilians including children to enable an immediate and unconditional ceasefire the release of the hostage and the massive scale up of the humanitarian operation in Gaza according to the principles of humanity neutrality impartiality and Independence on the same not on the same note we condemn all acts of terrorism and violence inflicted against civilians these are the fundamental reasons why Portugal supported the resolution voted last week. Mr. President, finally, let me reassure that Portugal continues to see value in the high-level international conference for the peaceful settlement of the question of Palestine and the implementation of the two-state solution, postponed because of the ongoing hostilities between Israel and Iran. Portugal calls for maximum restraint and for the resumption of dialogue and diplomacy to put an end to the dangerous military escalation going on in the region right now. We must turn the page and set the conditions for a peaceful resolution of the Palestinian question that is the epicenter of the instability in the Middle East. based on the UN resolutions on the matter, and set a clear and solid path to a Palestinian state fulfilling the two-state solution, living side by side with Israel in peace and security. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Portugal, and now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Mexico.

President, today's meeting on the disastrous humanitarian situation in Gaza once again testifies to the resounding failure of the Security Council to fulfill its primary responsibility. It is a clear reminder of the way in which the international community has failed to meet the goal of upholding international peace and avoiding humanity facing the devastation and atrocities of war. The veto cast on the 4th of June last on a resolution that demanded an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and the lifting of restrictions on humanitarian aid is a direct affront to the protection of human lives. This veto did not just block collective urgent action. It is also part of the measures that have led to one of the worst disasters in our era. This continues to prolong the unbearable suffering that the Palestinian people have been subjected to. While the overwhelming majority of member states of this organization advocated a and called out for a peaceful solution, and the consolidation of two states, Israel and Palestine. The multilateral system has seen itself paralyzed by special interests. As long as the indiscriminate use of the veto is kept in the Security Council, the UN will be held will be subjected to the stance of just one of its members. At this juncture, as has been repeatedly stated, we must rethink and redesign the way in which the council functions, and in particular, the use of the veto. While we are gathered here in this meeting, there are lives that continue to be destroyed. There are people dying. The international community cannot stand idly by, nor should we dehumanize the figures of the numbers of displaced persons, in addition to those injured and deceased. Mexico strongly condemned the attacks by Hamas on the 7th of October, 2023. No political or legal argument can justify the violence that was committed on that day. At the same time, we have stated on repeated occasions our unwavering rejection of the indiscriminate, disproportionate, and systematic attacks that the Palestinian civilian population and humanitarian personnel have been subjected to by Israel's armed forces. Over the last few months, we have borne witness to grave violations of international law, including atrocious crimes that cannot, nor must they be, ignored. Given these facts, Mexico reiterates its commitment to the unwavering respect for international law and to accountability. The violence that has been triggered over the last few days between Israel and Iran should not make us overlook, turn away from what is happening in Gaza. At this juncture, demanding respect for international law is more important than ever. Member States of the UN must demand that the parties involved in armed conflicts fulfil their ethical and legal obligations. Mexico also supports the tireless work carried out by UNRWA, the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees, in delivering humanitarian aid and alleviating people's suffering.
